risk_manifestation.mechanism: Harlow campus draws up to 71–150 MW from the UK Power Networks East-of-England zone, flagged as a severe 15-year delay region. risk_manifestation.insured_today: No evidence of a solar-generation contingent BI or private-wire supply failure rider on the campus programme. Standard PD/BI would not respond to a solar-output shortfall that is not caused by physical damage.

risk_manifestation.mechanism: Ark operates security-critical, MOD-adjacent infrastructure where tenants require near-100% availability. A grid or mechanical failure triggering an SLA breach could result in contractual penalties or re-siting costs that are not covered under standard PD/BI wordings (contractual liability exclusion is standard).
risk_manifestation.insured_today: PD/BI covers loss of gross profit from physical damage; SLA penalty payments and tenant migration costs are typically excluded. No evidence of contractual liability or SLA-mirror cover.
risk_manifestation.typical_gap: trigger_gap 1/4 — firm power and strong on-site backup reduce exposure, but SLA penalty gap persists

risk_manifestation.headline: Distributed estate — regional grid event correlates multiple sites
risk_manifestation.mechanism: Ark operates multiple UK campuses in the M4/Wiltshire corridor. A regional grid fault or extreme weather event affecting the South West transmission zone could simultaneously impact several sites, creating a correlated loss that exceeds any single-site BI aggregate.
risk_manifestation.insured_today: Property cat and BI programmes are structured per-site; multi-site correlation in a single grid zone is typically not explicitly priced or capped in standard wording.
risk_manifestation.typical_gap: aggregation_correlation 1/4 — distributed estate lowers per-site risk, but regional correlation is underpriced

grid_posture.dno: SP Energy Networks — Mersey / Cheshire region; 275kV direct transmission bay connection at Capenhurst substation, stacking active power, capacity, and voltage services
grid_posture.constraint_zone: Cheshire / Capenhurst — single 275kV transmission bay at SP Energy Networks; world-first reactive-power absorption from transmission

risk_manifestation.headline: ESO balancing de-dispatch — BESS revenue curtailment without damage
risk_manifestation.mechanism: The 100 MW / 107 MWh BESS earns revenue by stacking active-power, capacity, and voltage services. ESO balancing instructions or FFR/BM de-dispatch orders can reduce or suspend BESS dispatch without causing physical damage to the battery or plant. Revenue curtailment from a de-dispatch event is not a damage event and falls outside standard PD/BI scope.
risk_manifestation.insured_today: Standard property all-risks covers physical damage to battery modules and associated plant. BI cover responds to loss of gross profit following physical damage. A de-dispatch without physical damage does not trigger either. No parametric or availability product evidenced.
risk_manifestation.typical_gap: trigger_gap 3/4 — damage-only cover; de-dispatch revenue risk wholly uninsured

risk_manifestation.headline: 100 MW at one 275kV node — project-finance revenue covenant at risk
risk_manifestation.mechanism: The full 100 MW / 107 MWh is concentrated at a single Capenhurst 275kV transmission bay in the SP Energy Networks / Mersey region. A transmission fault, maintenance outage, or planned upgrade at that node would take the entire asset offline. Santander project-finance covenants rely on continuous revenue generation; an extended outage creates debt-service risk not backstopped by available cover.
risk_manifestation.insured_today: Property all-risks / BI would respond to physical damage causing the outage; a planned maintenance window or non-damage transmission restriction would not trigger. Project finance debt-service cover is not standard in BESS insurance programmes.
risk_manifestation.typical_gap: aggregation_correlation 4/4 — all revenue concentrated at one transmission node
